body: lsof says nothing is using it
Only one instance of syncthing running?

At a guess, this is the same as #241. Under some circumstances, which I have yet to narrow down, either the program exit is too slow or sockets linger around, so they are still in use when syncthing starts up again.

Background: the restart works like this...
1. Start a new instance of syncthing. An environment variable is set indicating that this is a restart.
2. The new syncthing instance sees the environment variable and pauses startup for about two seconds.
3. The old syncthing instance exits, closing it's sockets.
4. The new syncthing instance continues startup, opens the sockets.

Really, the listening sockets should probably be passed on to the new instance somehow...
What if you changed 2. to wait until 3. had finished?

Yeah. It's just more code, that's all. :)

(The simplest approach is usually best, until it's proven not to be ;)

I'm also seeing this a fair bit (1 time in 3 or so, if I use "restart" in the Web GUI) - I've been getting around it by manually shutting down the syncthing instance, and then waiting a few seconds before restarting.
Is it normal that lsof doesn't show something with the port open?
That _should_ work, but I can't really test it because I've been unable to reproduce the original issue.
Just for info (I know you fixed this already): killing syncthing, then waiting for an hour before starting it again didn't free the port!

Eh? That seems broken in some entirely different way. There's nothing socket wise that could/should survive that long. Sounds like there is more than one syncthing running, to be honest, or something else using the same port...

Nope, no firewalling. It's probably a "regular" lingering socket. The way it's implemented right now it checks if the listen port is free and then continues. That doesn't guarantee the GUI port is free yet though.
